newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: NEW NAFTA SUPERVISORY BOARD ELECTED.
newsitem.headline: NEW NAFTA SUPERVISORY BOARD ELECTED.

text.p: Shareholders of gas storage company Nafta a.s. elected a new supervisory board and dismissed the old one on Tuesday after a little-known company bought a stake from the state at a knock-down price.

Shareholders representing 65 percent of Nafta shares also approved at an extraordinary general meeting a change to the company's statutes, allowing a transfer of 49.5 percent of the company from the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), to Druha Obchodna a.s..
One of the owners of Druha Obchodna, Stefan Holan, 40, was elected to the new supervisory board.
Druha Obchodna bought the stake in August for 500 million crowns. It was worth around 3.2 billion crowns on the Bratislava Stock Exchange.

The new supervisory board has nine members as opposed to 12 members elected earlier this year. Five members including Holan were nominated by Druha Obchodna while three of the others are Nafta employees.
Nafta official Dana Vankova said the supervisory board would elect its chairman at a later meeting. "There were no discussion of changes to the company's management," she added.
No details of Druha Obchodna have been made available.
Foreign shareholders who held an estimated 20-30 percent of Nafta appeared to have been selling off of their holdings, brokers said.
